commits.edited_message:
lib: Call unknown encoding release before teardown

Signed-off-by: Junki Lee <junkilee80@gmail.com>


Now that the release callback is invoked from a single, well-defined point
at the very start of teardown, the defensive self-reset of
m_unknownEncodingRelease/m_unknownEncodingData inside
callUnknownEncodingRelease() is redundant and is dropped.

lib|tests: Handle OOM when copying encodingName in XML_ParserReset

When XML_ParserReset(parser, encodingName) is called with a non-NULL
encodingName, parserInit() invokes copyString() to allocate and store
the protocol encoding name. If memory allocation fails, copyString()
returns NULL.

Unlike parserCreate() and XML_SetEncoding(), which both check
(encodingName && ! parser->m_protocolEncodingName) and fail cleanly,
XML_ParserReset() previously ignored this allocation failure and returned
XML_TRUE. This silently dropped the requested encoding, leaving
m_protocolEncodingName as NULL while reporting success to the caller.

Check for this allocation failure in XML_ParserReset(), set
parser->m_errorCode to XML_ERROR_NO_MEMORY, and return XML_FALSE.
Also add a unit test test_alloc_reset_encoding in alloc_tests.c.


While here, move the one-time initialization of the unknown-encoding
release hook (m_unknownEncodingRelease) and its data pointer
(m_unknownEncodingData) out of parserInit() -- which is shared with
XML_ParserReset() -- and into parserCreate(), alongside the rest of the
parser's lifetime-scoped state. These pointers describe a one-time
association established by XML_SetUnknownEncodingHandler() and need not be
re-cleared on every reset.

coupling:
Heap double-free (CWE-415) of the application-owned unknown-encoding `data` buffer: Expat invokes the app's `info.release` callback twice for a single (data, release) pair -- once from XML_ParserReset() and again from XML_ParserFree(). On the base/original tree the release hook is cleared after the first teardown call by TWO independent, redundant resets, so the second teardown sees a NULL hook and does nothing:
  (S1) callUnknownEncodingRelease() self-clears m_unknownEncodingRelease/m_unknownEncodingData right after calling the hook (edited in commit 2d4032a), and
  (S2) parserInit() -- which XML_ParserReset() runs during teardown -- re-initializes the same two fields to NULL (edited in commit f25f79d, which relocates that one-time init into parserCreate()).
Commit f25f79d, read alone, is benign: it moves the release/data init from parserInit() to parserCreate() (fresh parsers are still initialized, so create+free is safe), and on a reset the still-present S1 self-clear keeps the single-release invariant. Commit 2d4032a, read alone, is benign: it drops the 'redundant' S1 self-clear, but the still-present S2 (parserInit re-NULLs on reset) keeps the invariant. ONLY when both edits combine does XML_ParserReset() leave m_unknownEncodingRelease/Data pointing at the already-released buffer, so the subsequent XML_ParserFree() calls the hook a second time -> double-free. A correct fix must restore AT LEAST ONE of the two resets while reasoning about the other: fixing only 2d4032a's diff (re-adding S1) OR only f25f79d's diff (keeping S2 in parserInit) each requires understanding that the other commit removed the complementary guard -- neither diff looks wrong in isolation. Reverting either edit alone makes the PoC pass cleanly (verified).
